question: The horizontal distance from the base of a flagpole to a wall is \(6\text{ m}\). The shadow of the top of the flagpole falls exactly on the wall, \(2\text{ m}\) above the ground. At the same time, a bamboo pole \(1\text{ m}\) long casts a shadow \(0.5\text{ m}\) long. Find the height of the flagpole. (Unit: m)
solution: The light rays descend \(1\text{ m}\) for every \(0.5\text{ m}\) forward, or \(2\text{ m}\) for every \(1\text{ m}\) horizontally. Over the horizontal distance of \(6\text{ m}\) from the top of the flagpole to the wall, they descend \(12\text{ m}\). Thus, the height of the flagpole is \(2+12=14\text{ m}\).
